entries.name: Philip J. Fry
entries.sourceWork: Futurama, série Fox originale (1999–2003), Fry livreur de Planet Express
entries.sourceReference: Fry is an ordinary Planet Express delivery boy in the original Fox run. A parcel relay and safe-position signal are bounded coordination adaptations, not ammunition, a parcel explosion, a laser attack or an invented psychic power. His red jacket, white shirt, blue jeans and orange hair are fixed to this period.
entries.characterVersion: Philip J. Fry from original Fox Futurama (1999–2003). Ordinary human young adult delivery boy, orange swept-pointed hair, red open waist-length jacket over plain white T-shirt, blue jeans, black-and-white sneakers. His only prop is a small plain brown delivery parcel, never a gun.

entries.name: Leela
entries.sourceWork: Futurama, série Fox originale (1999–2003), Leela pilote et combattante
entries.sourceReference: Leela is a skilled physical martial artist and Planet Express pilot. This short punch-and-kick combination uses her limbs and athletic guard, not a gun, laser or eye beam. One accepted close contact resolves damage; generated drawings do not add extra hits. Her single central eye remains a single eye.
entries.characterVersion: Turanga Leela from original Fox Futurama (1999–2003). Athletic adult female cyclops, EXACTLY ONE large central eye (never two eyes), long purple hair in high ponytail, white sleeveless tank top, black trousers, gray heavy boots, small wrist device on left wrist. Unarmed physical martial artist; no firearm or laser.

entries.name: Bender
entries.sourceWork: Futurama, série Fox originale (1999–2003), Bender Bending Rodríguez
entries.sourceReference: Bender is the gray bending robot from the original Fox run. Articulated arms, hands and a short physical charge stay mechanical. His chest compartment does not spawn weapons, his eyes do not fire beams and this authored contact sequence does not invent a plasma cannon.
entries.characterVersion: Bender Bending Rodriguez from original Fox Futurama (1999–2003). Original canonical silvery-gray cylindrical bending robot, square black eye visor containing TWO pale yellow round eyes, long mouth grill, single thin head antenna with ball tip, barrel torso and rectangular chest door, segmented flexible tube arms and legs, mechanical hands and broad robot feet. No clothes, gun, laser or human anatomy.

entries.name: Amy Wong
entries.sourceWork: Futurama, série Fox originale (1999–2003), Amy stagiaire ingénieure de Planet Express
entries.sourceReference: Amy is a Planet Express engineering intern in the original Fox period. Examining an ordinary handheld diagnostic pad and communicating a finding give bounded coordination buffs. She has no damaging scanner, gun, healing ray or magical repair power. The pink tracksuit and black bob haircut remain her normal outfit.
entries.characterVersion: Amy Wong from original Fox Futurama (1999–2003). Adult East Asian human woman with short neat black bob haircut and bangs, pink cropped tracksuit jacket over simple white shirt, matching pink jogging trousers, white sneakers. Ordinary Planet Express engineering intern. She carries a small compact gray diagnostic pad. No gun, laser, magical repair effect or healing symbol.

entries.name: Hermes Conrad
entries.sourceWork: Futurama, série Fox originale (1999–2003), Hermes bureaucrate de Planet Express
entries.sourceReference: Hermes is the human bureaucrat of Planet Express. He sorts actual papers, checks a clipboard and gives work instructions. These zero-damage coordination effects do not turn paperwork, limbo or spoken orders into lasers, physical projectiles, instant healing or supernatural barriers.
entries.characterVersion: Hermes Conrad from original Fox Futurama (1999–2003). Stocky adult Jamaican human bureaucrat with medium-dark brown skin, short black dreadlocks, small glasses, green office jacket and green trousers, white collared shirt and orange tie, brown shoes. He holds plain clipboard and paper sheets, not a weapon. No laser or magical effect.

entries.name: Zoidberg
entries.sourceWork: Futurama, série Fox originale (1999–2003), Dr John Zoidberg
entries.sourceReference: Dr John Zoidberg is the red Decapodian in a white medical coat, mint shirt and gray trousers. This version uses cautious advice and withdrawal signals rather than claiming reliable human treatment. No HP regeneration, healing magic, claw projectile or beam is supplied by these gestures.
entries.characterVersion: Dr John Zoidberg from original Fox Futurama (1999–2003). No human fingers or extra arms. Plain medical clipboard only. No healing aura, cross symbol, weapon, magic or beam.

entries.name: Rick Sanchez
entries.sourceWork: Rick and Morty, saison 2 (2015), Rick Sanchez humain
entries.sourceReference: Season2 Rick uses an ordinary compact science-fiction pistol as the selected damaging equipment. The distinct green portal gun is a transit device and is not used as a damaging blaster. The support action communicates a safe route without teleporting units, splitting reality or creating a Microverse explosion. His source-era white coat, pale cyan shirt and brown trousers remain unchanged.
entries.characterVersion: Rick Sanchez in Rick and Morty SEASON TWO (2015), biological human elderly scientist. Spiky pale blue hair and matching unibrow, long thin face, white lab coat, pale turquoise shirt, brown trousers, dark belt, black shoes. He carries ONE compact ordinary gray science-fiction hand PISTOL with short horizontal barrel, visibly separate from his green rectangular portal gun. Do NOT draw the green portal device, portals or green magical rays. No cybernetic variants.

entries.name: Summer Smith
entries.sourceWork: Rick and Morty, saison 2 (2015), Summer Smith avant la tenue post-apocalyptique de saison 3

entries.name: Birdperson
entries.sourceWork: Rick and Morty, saison 2 (2015), Birdperson avant sa transformation en Phoenixperson
entries.sourceReference: Birdperson is his biological season2 version before Phoenixperson. His natural brown feathered wings fold into a physical protective stance, adapted into a bounded guard without adding flight, teleportation, healing or a supernatural force field. Cybernetic wings, implants, laser eyes and the later Phoenixperson weapons are excluded.
entries.characterVersion: Birdperson from Rick and Morty SEASON TWO (2015), standard biological pre-Phoenixperson version. Canonical adult bird-human with long dark hair, long angular face and prominent beak-like nose, his familiar white feather cap/headpiece, bare upper torso, green trousers, birdlike feet and large NATURAL brown feathered wings. Keep recognizable original series design, wings attached at shoulder/back, not mechanical. No tuxedo, implants, cybernetics, laser, gun or Phoenixperson armor.
